newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SEPT SOC.SEC, DEFICIT WIDENS TO HUF62.5BLN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SEPT SOC.SEC, DEFICIT WIDENS TO HUF62.5BLN.

text.p: Hungary's social security deficit widened to 62.2 billion forints in September from 56 billion forints at the end of August, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
Hungary's social security deficit target for 1996 is 17.8 billion forints.

Finance Ministry Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told a news conference on Tuesday that the bloating social security deficit was not likely to threaten the government budget deficit target, four percent of the GDP, agreed with the International Monetary Fund in March.

"My opinion is that the government budget deficit will be four percent," Laszlo said, adding that larger-than-planned central state budget revenues were likely to provide compensation for the social security's losses.
The government budget includes the central state budget, the social security budget and other items.
Hungary's central state budget deficit stood at 75.5 billion forints at the end of October, compared with the 232.9 billion forint target for 1996.
However, the budget deficit was likely to widen substantially in November and December, due to seasonal factors including debt service, Laszlo said.

The total government budget deficit for 1996 might be some fifteen billion forints higher or lower than the target as certain revenues and expenditures of November and December could be calculated only roughly, he added.
